questionText:
An articulation point in a connected graph is a vertex such that removing the vertex and its incident edges disconnects the graph into two or more connected components.

Let $T$ be a DFS tree obtained by doing DFS in a connected undirected graph $G$. Which of the following options is/are correct?
options: Root of $T$ can never be an articulation point in $G$.
Root of $T$ is an articulation point in $G$ if and only if it has 2 or more children.
A leaf of $T$ can be an articulation point in $G$.
If $u$ is an articulation point in $G$ such that $x$ is an ancestor of $u$ in $T$ and $y$ is a descendent of $u$ in $T$, then all paths from $x$ to $y$ in $G$ must pass through $u$.
explanation:
Analysis of Statements:

1. Option (A) and Option (B):
In a Depth-First Search (DFS) tree $T$ of a connected undirected graph $G$:
• The root of $T$ is an articulation point in $G$ if and only if it has at least 2 children in $T$.
• If the root has only 1 child, removing the root leaves the single subtree connected, so it is not an articulation point.
• If the root has 2 or more children, there can be no edge connecting the different subtrees (due to DFS tree properties in undirected graphs). Thus, removing the root disconnects these subtrees.
Hence, Option (A) is FALSE and Option (B) is CORRECT.

2. Option (C):
Let $v$ be a leaf in the DFS tree $T$.
• In an undirected graph, all non-tree edges are back-edges to ancestors.
• Since $v$ is a leaf, removing $v$ leaves $T \setminus \{v\}$ as a connected spanning tree for all remaining vertices $V \setminus \{v\}$.
• Therefore, removing a leaf can never disconnect $G \setminus \{v\}$.
Hence, Option (C) is FALSE.

3. Option (D):
• Even if $u$ is an articulation point in $G$, it separates specific subtrees, but not necessarily every descendant $y$ from an ancestor $x$.
• If a descendant $y$ has a back-edge directly to $x$ (or an ancestor above $u$), there exists a path from $x$ to $y$ bypassing $u$. As long as $u$ separates another subtree from the rest of the graph, $u$ remains an articulation point, but the path between this specific $x$ and $y$ does not pass through $u$.
Hence, Option (D) is FALSE.

Conclusion:
Only Option (B) is correct.
